subject: Request: DPA carveouts for runtime telemetry / subprocessors — product & security input needed
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Cassandra Li <cass@splitwave.ai>, SplitWave Procurement <procurement@splitwave.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: runtime telemetry carveout proposal + subprocessors list (redline attached)

Hi Cassandra / procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive conversation last week. Attached is our suggested redline (redlined_dpa_v3.pdf) and the current subprocessors export. Two asks on our side that need internal product/security confirmation before we can finalize:

1) Runtime telemetry carveout: your legal team has requested explicit carveouts for certain runtime artifacts (KV cache snapshots, per-request token traces, and temporary prefix caches). The goal from SplitWave is to limit what leaves the runtime for analytics. We are proposing the following language in the DPA: runtime-level ephemeral artifacts used for inference ("KV cache snapshots" and "temporary request traces") are excluded from analytics exports and are retained only transiently for request fulfilment unless customer explicitly opts in.

- Why this matters (brief): our serving runtime uses per-request KV caches and prefix caches that may contain model context fragments. Excluding these from exports protects customer prompt content while still allowing aggregated telemetry (latency, throughput, error rates).

2) Subprocessors: we've included our current subprocessors CSV for your review. SplitWave asked for a 30-day notice for material changes and an allowlist option for exportable telemetry.

Internal ask to Olga / Priya / Mateo: can Security & Product confirm feasibility and proposed mitigations by end of day tomorrow? Specifically:
- Security: can you sign off on the proposed carveout language (or propose precise alternative wording) so legal can accept? If not, what additional controls are required (e.g., WORM retention, HSM-bound keys for telemetry buckets, hashed-only metadata)?
- Product/Eng (Mateo): is there an engineering path to: (a) flag telemetry exports to exclude KV/prefix cache contents, (b) provide a customer toggle at the account level (hosted + dedicated) to opt-out of request-level telemetry, and (c) estimate implementation effort and timeline?

Attachments: redlined_dpa_v3.pdf (annotated), subprocessors_list_splitwave.csv

Proposed next steps: internal sign-off -> send final DPA to SplitWave for countersign (DocuSign link in related_links) -> procurement closes.

Cassandra — wanted to be transparent on the blockers; if we can get a technical/wording path quickly we can meet your procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Cassandra Li <cass@splitwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: runtime telemetry carveout proposal + subprocessors list (redline attached)

Thanks Tessa — looping legal/security input in-line.

Short answer: the carveout concept is reasonable, but legal needs clear operational guarantees. From security perspective we need the following as part of any carveout acceptance:
- A defined retention window (e.g., <= 72 hours) for any transient artifacts and a guarantee that exports for analytics do not contain unredacted prompt text.
- Hashing/pseudonymization for request IDs before being written to long-term telemetry stores.
- An auditable control path showing where the flag to include/exclude telemetry is enforced (console + API).
- For allowlist/notice on subprocessors, procurement-level SLA that changes are notified 30 days in advance and critical subprocessor additions require bilateral sign-off.

If product can deliver an account-level toggle and engineering can show retention enforcement and hashing, legal can offer alternative DPA language along the lines of: "Customer data for runtime ephemeral caches is excluded from analytics exports. Customer may enable exports via explicit account configuration. Any temporary artifacts are deleted within 72 hours and are pseudonymized in any long-term stores."

Please confirm timeline from Mateo so we can draft the precise clause.

- Olga
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

---

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Cassandra Li <cass@splitwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: runtime telemetry carveout proposal + subprocessors list (redline attached)

Hi team — quick engineering feasibility note.

Summary: All three asks are implementable, with tradeoffs. Details below.

1) Account-level telemetry toggle (hosted + dedicated): doable. We already have feature flags per-account for debug logging; extending to the telemetry export path is ~2 sprints (3 weeks) to add the flag + 1 sprint (1 week) for QA and rollout. We can make the default = enabled for existing customers and default = disabled for new customers who sign DPAs with carveouts. The toggle will: gate the export pipeline and remove payload fields (KV/prefix cache blobs) before any downstream store.

2) Retention enforcement and pseudonymization: we can add a 72-hour TTL on intermediate buckets and implement SHA-256 hashing of request identifiers before writing to long-term metrics. ETA: 2 sprints for retention automation + 1 sprint for PR/final QA. This requires infra changes to our telemetry pipeline (small infra infra work) and documentation updates.

3) Subprocessor notice/allowlist: operationally straightforward — procurement + account teams can push 30-day-notice changes. For critical subprocessor additions (e.g., new analytics vendor for event store) we can implement a workflow where the account receives an email and console notification; formal bilateral sign-off will require Legal/Procurement to mark as critical.

Potential product tradeoffs: removing request-level telemetry will reduce our ability to triage certain production edge cases (hard-to-reproduce prompts) and will limit some Optimize recommendations (prompt-level anomaly detection). We should scope which telemetry is required for SLA debugging vs analytics.

Proposed compromise: ship the account toggle + retention/pseudonymization in the timeline above (~5–6 weeks), and in parallel update our incident triage playbook to use aggregated metrics + signed customer one-time debug sessions (opt-in). That gives legal the guarantees they want while minimizing product risk.

I'll open a short RFC and link it here by EOD; we can attach acceptance criteria so Olga / Priya can translate to DPA language.

- Mateo
Senior Product Manager, Serving
Redwood Inference

---

From: Cassandra Li <cass@splitwave.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: SplitWave Procurement <procurement@splitwave.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: runtime telemetry carveout proposal + subprocessors list (redline attached)

Tessa / team — thanks for the quick responses and the pragmatic compromise. The timeline you proposed is acceptable to our procurement team provided we get a short-term bridge: can Redwood provide an interim written attestation that (a) exports will exclude unredacted prompt text immediately and (b) any subprocessor changes will come with 30 days notice? That will let procurement proceed to internal approval while your engineering changes are delivered.

If you can send an interim attestation (one paragraph) and a target delivery window for the toggles, we can proceed with countersign.

Best,
Cassandra Li
Head of Procurement, SplitWave AI
